sentences.text: Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant/accused,
relating to FIR/Crime No.41/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Badod,
District Agar Malwa for commission of offence punishable under Sections 406, 409, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
2 .

sentences.text: Prosecution story in brief is that on 04.03.2023, the complainant Samrath Jain lodged an FIR stating that Manish Jain is proprietor and son of complainant Rahul Jain is partner in the firm of complainant named Savariya Traders, which is involved in grain trade.
The applicant/accused is driver of truck bearing registration No.RJ-40-FGA-3697.

On 01.03.2023, at around 09:30 PM, the complainant loaded 251 quintals in 308 sacks of mustard amounting to a sum of Rs.13,42,800/-

sentences.text: Complainant had given advance of Rs.40,000/- to the applicant as truck freight charges.
The goods did not reach the destination.
Phone of the applicant could not be reached, being switched off.
Aforementioned truck was owned by Jaanu @ Jaan Mohammad from Alwar, Rajasthan.
An FIR was lodged against the applicant on 04.03.2023.

During investigation, it was found that real name of the applicant is Natthi Khan and real registration number of the aforementioned truck was RJ-14-GL-2880, but the applicant removed the original registration plate and placed an incorrect registration plate.

Thereby,
the applicant committed cheating with the complainant and also criminal breach of trust.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
No mustard is seized from the applicant.
The offence is triable by the Judicial Magistrate First Class.
Applicant is in custody since 21.03.2023.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and submits that co-accused Jaanu @ Jaan Mohammad is absconding till date.
Alleged goods and vehicle is to be recovered.
As per allegation, offence u/S 409 is also made out against the applicant.

The applicant has criminal antecedents, Crime No.378/2021, offence punishable u/S 420, 407,
120-B of IPC is registered in Alwar, Rajasthan and a Crime No.81/2013, offence punishable u/S 406 of IPC is registered in Maharashtra.
Applicant is resident of Rajasthan, he may even abscond on getting the benefit of bail therefore, the applicant is not entitled for bail.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case- diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, at this stage, this Court is of the view it is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, application for bail is dismissed.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE gp Yasin @ Asin @ Nathi Kha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140206100/
